summary.text: Mario Diaz-Balart is the Republican incumbent in Florida's 26th District. A Fort Lauderdale native, he began in public service as an aide to the Miami mayor, served in the Florida House and Senate in the 1990s and early 2000s, and has been in the U.S. House since 2003. He serves on the Appropriations Committee and is the dean of Florida's congressional delegation.

paragraphs.text: Born in Fort Lauderdale, Florida, on September 25, 1961, to Cuban parents; his father, Rafael Díaz-Balart, was a Cuban politician, and his brother Lincoln Díaz-Balart represented a Miami-area district in Congress from 1993 to 2011.
Studied political science at the University of South Florida.
Began his public service career in 1985 as an aide to the Mayor of Miami.

Served in the Florida State Senate (District 37) from 1992 to 2000, and in the Florida House of Representatives (District 112) from 2000 to 2002; Wikipedia also says he was elected to the Florida House in 1988.
Elected to the U.S. House in 2002 and has served since 2003 under successive district numbers as Florida's maps changed; has represented the 26th District since 2023.
In the 2025-2026 Congress, serves on the House Appropriations Committee as Vice Chair and chairs the subcommittee on National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs.
Has been the dean of Florida's congressional delegation since April 2021, according to Wikipedia.
